sections.h2: What should you know before selling a house in Kentwood, Michigan?
sections.html:
Kentwood sits in Kent County on the southeast side of Grand Rapids, and a sale there follows Michigan's county recording rules plus a few city offices you will deal with directly. The Census Bureau counts 54,776 residents for July 1, 2025, up 0.8 percent from the 2020 base, which makes Kentwood a steady market rather than a shrinking one.

Most sellers meet three questions early: what the house might fetch, what the city requires before title moves, and how the tax bill is split at closing. This page answers each with Kentwood's own figures and offices, so you can compare a traditional listing, a for-sale-by-owner sale and a cash offer from an investor on equal terms.

sections.h2: How is Kentwood laid out, and what does that mean for a home sale?
sections.html:
Kentwood covers about 21 square miles of land and is bordered by Wyoming on the west, Grand Rapids and Grand Rapids Township to the north, Cascade Township to the east and Gaines Township to the south. It was incorporated in 1967 out of Paris Township, partly to stop neighboring cities from annexing more land, and it took its name from the Kentwood Public Schools.

Road access shapes how quickly buyers can reach a house. The main routes are:

  • I-96, which clips the northeast corner of the city
  • M-11 along 28th Street, a busy commercial strip
  • M-37 along East Beltline Avenue and Broadmoor Avenue
  • M-6, the southern bypass linking I-196 near Hudsonville with I-96 near the Gerald R. Ford International Airport

Two paths, the Paul Henry Rail Trail and the East-West Trail, run through town, and homes near them tend to be easy to describe in a listing. School boundaries matter too: Kentwood Public Schools serves most addresses, while Forest Hills Public Schools and Kelloggsville Public Schools cover parts of the city. Check the district for your street before you set a price.

sections.h2: What do the Census numbers say about Kentwood housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 figures describe a city where owners are the majority and median rent runs $1,260 a month. The table lists the figures that bear most on a sale.

About four in ten homes are rented, so many Kentwood sellers are landlords, and the next section covers the rental certificate that affects them. A median value is a midpoint for the whole city. It will not predict your street, so ask for sold comparables from the same school attendance area.

sections.h2: Does winter in Kentwood affect what buyers look for?
sections.html:
Yes, because Kentwood has a warm-summer continental climate with real cold. Mean daily highs in January sit near 30 degrees Fahrenheit and mean lows near 15, and the area gets roughly 34 inches of precipitation across a year, spread fairly evenly from month to month.

Buyers and their inspectors therefore look hard at the furnace, attic insulation, the roof and the basement. If any of those are tired, you have two choices: spend before listing, or sell as-is at a price that reflects the work. An as-is cash sale shifts that repair risk to the buyer, which is the main reason some owners choose it. Whatever route you take, get the furnace serviced and keep the receipt, because heating questions come up first in almost every walkthrough.

sections.h2: Does a rental house in Kentwood need a certificate before it changes hands?
sections.html:
A rental dwelling in Kentwood must be registered and hold a valid certificate of compliance, and that certificate stays with the owner who earned it. Under the city's rental dwelling inspection ordinance, a certificate can pass to a buyer only if the sale closes within 90 days of the certificate being issued and the buyer tells the city within 30 days of the sale.

The details that matter to a landlord seller:

  • A six-year certificate does not transfer. If it moves to a new owner inside the 90-day window it reverts to a two-year certificate.
  • Failure by the buyer to notify the city results in suspension of the certificate, and a replacement is dated back to the sale with fees owed from that date.
  • An owner who lives in a condominium unit needs no registration or certification, but a condominium owned as a rental is treated as a single-family rental.
  • Certificates cannot be issued while the property has unpaid city bills.

Call the Inspections Department at 616-554-0700 before you sign a contract on a rental, so the certificate dates and any open violations are known in advance.

sections.h2: When are Kentwood property taxes due, and how do appeals work?
sections.html:
Kentwood mails summer bills in the first week of July, due August 20, and winter bills in the first week of December, due February 14. Anything still unpaid moves to the Kent County Treasurer on March 1, and summer deferments for qualifying owners must be filed with the city treasurer by September 15.

The assessment side runs on a fixed yearly rhythm:

  • Change notices go out soon after February 1 and carry the appeal dates.
  • The Board of Review begins hearings on the Tuesday after the first Monday in March, by appointment.
  • A residential owner who stays unhappy can file with the Michigan Tax Tribunal by July 31, after first appealing to the board.
  • A principal residence exemption affidavit must be on file by June 1 for the summer bill and November 1 for the winter bill.

Appeals cannot rest on a neighbor's lower tax bill. Michigan lets taxable value rise more slowly for long-term owners, so a recent buyer will usually pay more than an owner next door who has held the house for years.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill and the exemption after a Kentwood sale?
sections.html:
The buyer, not the seller, must file the state's property transfer affidavit with the Kentwood Assessor within 45 days of the transfer. Michigan law resets taxable value to the state equalized value in the year after a transfer of ownership, so the buyer's bill can differ sharply from yours.

As the seller, stop claiming your principal residence exemption by filing the rescission form with the city within 90 days of moving out. If you bought another Michigan home first and yours is still on the market, the city describes a conditional rescission that can keep the exemption for up to three tax years, but only if the house is not rented. Form 4640 from the state treasury covers it.

Deeds are recorded at the Kent County Register of Deeds at 300 Monroe Avenue NW in Grand Rapids. State transfer tax is $3.75 for each $500 of value, and the county tax is 55 cents per $500 in any county with fewer than 2,000,000 residents. Several exemptions exist, including transfers to a child or grandchild, so ask your title company which one applies.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale compare with listing in Kentwood?
sections.html:
A cash sale trades a higher possible price for speed and fewer conditions. A listing exposes the house to the widest set of buyers, but it comes with showings, inspections and financing contingencies that can fall through.

Before you accept any offer, write down what you need from the closing: a date, a payoff figure for the mortgage and a plan for tenants if there are any. Ask each buyer for a written offer that states who pays recording costs and transfer tax, and whether the buyer takes over open city violations. Pull the city's recent qualified sales from the Assessor's online search to check whether an offer falls near a reasonable range for your street.

faqs.q: How much does the Census say a Kentwood house is worth?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 median value for owner-occupied homes in Kentwood is $268,200. Treat it as a citywide midpoint and compare it with sold prices on your own block.

faqs.q: Who collects Kentwood property tax, and where do unpaid taxes go?
faqs.a: The Kentwood Treasurer collects summer taxes due August 20 and winter taxes due February 14. Unpaid taxes move to the Kent County Treasurer on March 1.

faqs.q: Do I have to file anything with the city after I sell?
faqs.a: The buyer files the property transfer affidavit within 45 days. You should file the principal residence exemption rescission within 90 days of moving out, and a landlord should confirm the rental certificate transfer with Inspections.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Kentwood rental with tenants still living there?
faqs.a: Yes, but the rental certificate must be valid and the buyer must notify the city within 30 days of the sale for a transferred certificate to stay in force. Call Inspections at 616-554-0700 first.

faqs.q: Which county office records the deed for a Kentwood sale?
faqs.a: The Kent County Register of Deeds records it at 300 Monroe Avenue NW in Grand Rapids. State and county transfer tax are due when the deed is recorded unless an exemption applies.
